# What you end up with

<!-- Generated by `yarn docs`. Rendered from the generators themselves, so it cannot drift;
     a test fails if this file and the code disagree. Do not edit by hand. -->

Everything on this page is what `ever-better bootstrap` actually writes, rendered by the same
code that writes it. Yours will differ where your repository does — the framework, the package
manager, and whether it is TypeScript yet.

Every file is yours after it is written. The one rule is that softening a rule to clear a red
build is the wrong move: the suppressions file already granted every exception that was
justified.

## Configuration

### eslint.config.js — plain TypeScript, Node

Every rule is an error. Whatever exists when you freeze is grandfathered.

```js
// Generated by ever-better. This file is yours — edit it.
//
// Every rule below is an ERROR, and every violation that existed when you ran
// `ever-better freeze` is recorded in eslint-suppressions.json. Old code is grandfathered;
// new code is held to the whole standard from the first commit. Do not soften a rule to make
// a red build green — the suppressions file already did that, once, on purpose.
//
// Type assertions are banned outright: `as`, `<T>x`, `!`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck`. Each is a
// claim the compiler could not check and that no reviewer can see. Write a type guard instead —
// `const isThing = (v: unknown): v is Thing => ...` — which is testable, narrows for every
// caller, and fails at the boundary where the data was actually wrong.

import js from "@eslint/js";
import globals from "globals";
import tseslint from "typescript-eslint";
import sonarjs from "eslint-plugin-sonarjs";
import prettierRecommended from "eslint-plugin-prettier/recommended";
import security from "eslint-plugin-security";

export default tseslint.config(
  { ignores: ["dist/**", "build/**", "coverage/**", "node_modules/**", ".vercel/**"] },
  {
    linterOptions: {
      reportUnusedDisableDirectives: "error",
    },
  },

  js.configs.recommended,
  // strictTypeChecked, not recommended: the type-aware rules that find real bugs are only in
  // the TypeChecked presets, and the strict variant is where the `any` family lives.
  tseslint.configs.strictTypeChecked,
  // The two are disjoint; typescript-eslint's own advice is to use both.
  tseslint.configs.stylisticTypeChecked,
  {
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: { projectService: true, tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname },
    },
  },
  sonarjs.configs.recommended,
  security.configs.recommended,
  prettierRecommended,

  { languageOptions: { globals: globals.node } },

  {
    // Types as a second rule set. `any` and `!` are how a type system gets talked out of
    // doing its job, and both are invisible in review.
    rules: {
      "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "error",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion": "error",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": ["error", { argsIgnorePattern: "^__" }],
      // A private field nothing reassigns is a constant, and saying so stops the next reader
      // looking for the write that never happens.
      "@typescript-eslint/prefer-readonly": "error",
      // `as` asserts what the compiler could not check, and it is invisible in review. Write a
      // type guard instead — the guard is testable and the assertion is a promise.
      "@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions": ["error", { assertionStyle: "never" }],
      // The other doors out of the type system. `@ts-expect-error` survives only with a
      // written reason, because it is the one that fails loudly when it stops being needed.
      "@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment": [
        "error",
        {
          "ts-ignore": true,
          "ts-nocheck": true,
          "ts-check": false,
          "ts-expect-error": "allow-with-description",
          minimumDescriptionLength: 10,
        },
      ],
    },
  },
  {
    rules: {
      // typescript-eslint enables both of these for `.ts` files only, so the JavaScript repo
      // that actually contains `var` is the one nothing checks — and `.jsx`, `.vue` and `.mjs`
      // stay uncovered after a migration. `eslint --fix` converts the lot: var -> let, then
      // let -> const everywhere nothing reassigns.
      "no-var": "error",
      "prefer-const": "error",
      // A reassigned parameter makes the argument name lie for the rest of the function, and
      // the caller cannot see it happen.
      "no-param-reassign": "error",
    },
  },
  {
    // Size and complexity guards. These are the ones that turn into refactoring work rather
    // than one-line fixes, which is exactly why they are recorded rather than negotiated.
    rules: {
      "max-lines": ["error", { max: 600, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],
      "max-lines-per-function": ["error", { max: 50, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],
      complexity: ["error", 15],
      "max-depth": ["error", 4],
      "max-nested-callbacks": ["error", 4],
      "max-params": ["error", 6],
      "sonarjs/cognitive-complexity": ["error", 15],
    },
  },
  {
    rules: {
      // A `return` inside the `if` makes the `else` a level of indentation nobody needs.
      "no-else-return": ["error", { allowElseIf: false }],
      // Two `if`s that are one `&&`: a level of nesting for no extra branch.
      "sonarjs/no-collapsible-if": "error",
    },
  },
  {
    rules: {
      // A loop counter and a discarded binding are not what this is aimed at; a variable called
      // `d` holding a customer record is. `js`, `fs`, `os` are the conventional module aliases.
      "id-length": [
        "error",
        { min: 3, exceptions: ["_", "i", "j", "k", "id", "ok", "to", "up", "js", "fs", "os"] },
      ],
    },
  },
  {
    // A spec repeats itself by nature and its length is not a comprehension problem.
    files: ["test/**"],
    rules: {
      "max-lines": "off",
      "max-lines-per-function": "off",
      "sonarjs/no-duplicate-string": "off",
    },
  },
  {
    files: ["**/*.config.js", "**/*.config.mjs", "**/*.config.cjs"],
    languageOptions: { parserOptions: { projectService: false } },
    ...tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked,
  },
);
```

### eslint.config.js — Vue

`.vue` is wired into the type program, and the unsafe-any family is off for SFCs because ESLint's type program cannot generate component types.

```js

//
// Every rule below is an ERROR, and every violation that existed when you ran
// `ever-better freeze` is recorded in eslint-suppressions.json. Old code is grandfathered;
// new code is held to the whole standard from the first commit. Do not soften a rule to make
// a red build green — the suppressions file already did that, once, on purpose.
//
// Type assertions are banned outright: `as`, `<T>x`, `!`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck`. Each is a
// claim the compiler could not check and that no reviewer can see. Write a type guard instead —
// `const isThing = (v: unknown): v is Thing => ...` — which is testable, narrows for every
// caller, and fails at the boundary where the data was actually wrong.

import js from "@eslint/js";
import globals from "globals";
import tseslint from "typescript-eslint";
import sonarjs from "eslint-plugin-sonarjs";
import prettierRecommended from "eslint-plugin-prettier/recommended";
import security from "eslint-plugin-security";
import pluginVue from "eslint-plugin-vue";

export default tseslint.config(
  { ignores: ["dist/**", "build/**", "coverage/**", "node_modules/**", ".vercel/**"] },
  {
    linterOptions: {
      reportUnusedDisableDirectives: "error",
    },
  },

  js.configs.recommended,
  // strictTypeChecked, not recommended: the type-aware rules that find real bugs are only in
  // the TypeChecked presets, and the strict variant is where the `any` family lives.
  tseslint.configs.strictTypeChecked,
  // The two are disjoint; typescript-eslint's own advice is to use both.
  tseslint.configs.stylisticTypeChecked,
  {
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: { projectService: true, tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname },
    },
  },
  sonarjs.configs.recommended,
  security.configs.recommended,
  ...pluginVue.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    files: ["**/*.vue"],
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: {
        parser: tseslint.parser,
        // Without this the type program refuses .vue outright, and every component
        // reports an unsuppressable parse error.
        extraFileExtensions: [".vue"],
      },
    },
    rules: {
      // A component called Button.vue is one word on purpose.
      "vue/multi-word-component-names": "off",
    },
  },
  {
    // The `any` family is off wherever a .vue component type is in play. This is a limit of
    // the linter, not a hole in the code — vue-tsc still checks it.
    //
    // A .ts file that imports a type or component FROM a .vue inherits the same blind spot.
    // Add it to this list with the import named, so the entry can be deleted if the type
    // program ever learns SFCs.
    files: ["**/*.vue"],
    rules: {
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-argument": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-call": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-member-access": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-return": "off",

      "@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment": [

          "ts-nocheck": true,
          "ts-check": false,

  },
  {

### eslint.config.js — JavaScript, before migrating

The type-aware tier is absent because it cannot run. Migrating unlocks the half that finds real bugs.

```js

### knip.json

Entry points only where the file exists — knip prints a hint for every pattern matching nothing, and a first run full of complaints about itself does not get read again.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/knip@6/schema.json",
  "entry": [
    "src/index.ts",
    "test/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}"
  ],
  "project": [
    "src/**/*.ts"
  ],
  "rules": {
    "exports": "warn",
    "types": "warn",
    "files": "warn",
    "dependencies": "warn",
    "devDependencies": "warn",
    "unlisted": "warn",
    "binaries": "warn"
  }
}
```

### .gitattributes

Without it, Windows checks out CRLF and every formatter reports the whole repository as wrong — on one runner only.

```text
# Generated by ever-better.
#
# Without `eol=lf`, Windows checks out CRLF and every formatter and linter reports the whole
# repository as wrong — a failure that appears on one runner only.
* text=auto eol=lf

*.png binary
*.jpg binary
*.jpeg binary
*.gif binary
*.ico binary
*.woff binary
*.woff2 binary
*.pdf binary
```

## tsconfig.json

`bootstrap` does not write a tsconfig; it adds the strictness flags `strict: true` does **not**
include, and only the ones that cost nothing. Type errors have no suppression mechanism —
`--suppress-all` cannot touch them — so a flag that costs 500 errors would leave you with a
failing `typecheck` and no way to stage the work.

Each flag is priced by enabling it in a temporary config that extends yours and counting the
errors. Measured on a real fixture:

```
Enabled at zero cost: exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitReturns,
                      noFallthroughCasesInSwitch, noImplicitOverride,
                      noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature
Priced and left off — each is a task, not a flag flip:
  noUncheckedIndexedAccess: 1 type errors — left off
```

Applied to your file by inserting after the `"compilerOptions": {` anchor — never by parsing and
re-serialising, because a tsconfig is usually JSONC and a round trip would delete the comments
explaining why the other options are there:

```jsonc
{
  // hand-written comment that survives
  "compilerOptions": {
    // Enabled by ever-better after measuring each at zero new type errors.
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "noImplicitOverride": true,
    "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true,
    "target": "ES2022",
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

## Workflows

### .github/workflows/ci.yml

Three platforms. Path handling and file watching break per platform, and only per platform.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. Edit freely.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: lint
        run: yarn lint
      - name: typecheck
        run: yarn typecheck
      - name: build
        run: yarn build
      - name: test
        run: yarn test
```

### .github/workflows/ever-better.yml

The gate, in its own file so nothing has to edit a pipeline this tool did not write.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. Its own workflow on purpose: adding a step to a pipeline this
# tool did not write would mean editing YAML it cannot parse.
name: ever-better

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    name: ever-better check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: ever-better check
        run: npx --yes ever-better check --no-write

      # `always()`: the run where check has just failed is the run where knowing what the
      # backlog looks like is worth most. A report is not a gate and never changes the result.
      - name: ever-better report
        if: always()
        run: npx --yes ever-better report
```

### .github/workflows/codex-review.yml

Skips itself green without an API key — a check that is red until somebody adds a secret is one everybody learns to ignore.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. A second model reviews every pull request.
#
# Needs an OPENAI_API_KEY repository secret. Without it the job reports that and passes —
# a check that is red until somebody adds a secret is a check everyone learns to ignore.
name: codex-review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: codex-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CODEX_VERSION: "0.125.0"

jobs:
  codex-review:
    # Dependabot pull requests receive no repository secrets, so the key would resolve to an
    # empty string and the review would fail seconds in. A version bump gains nothing from it.
    if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write # to post the review as a comment
    steps:
      - name: Check for the API key
        id: key
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::OPENAI_API_KEY is not set — skipping the Codex review."
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        if: steps.key.outputs.present == 'true'
        with:
          # Codex needs the full history to diff the pull request.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        if: steps.key.outputs.present == 'true'
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install the Codex CLI
        if: steps.key.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: npm install -g "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}"

      - name: Review
        if: steps.key.outputs.present == 'true'
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git diff "$BASE"...HEAD > /tmp/pr.diff
          codex exec --skip-git-repo-check \
            "Review the diff between the base branch and HEAD of this pull request. Report only defects you can point at: a wrong result, an unhandled failure, a race, a security hole. Skip style — a formatter and a linter already ran. End with exactly one line: `CODEX VERDICT: LGTM` or `CODEX VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED`." \
            < /tmp/pr.diff > /tmp/review.md
          cat /tmp/review.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          gh pr comment "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" --body-file /tmp/review.md
```

### .github/workflows/duplication-scan.yml

Report-only. A global duplication percentage cannot catch new duplication; SARIF into Code Scanning gives the per-PR view.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. Report-only: a check that cannot point at what THIS diff added
# must not gate, or the first false failure teaches everyone to reach for an ignore comment.
name: duplication-scan

on:
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  duplication-scan:
    name: Duplication Scan (jscpd)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write # required to upload SARIF
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Run jscpd
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx --yes jscpd@4 . \
            --format "typescript,javascript,jsx,tsx,vue" \
            --ignore "**/node_modules/**,**/dist/**,**/build/**,**/*.d.ts" \
            --reporters console,sarif \
            --output report

      - name: Upload SARIF to Code Scanning
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4
        with:
          sarif_file: report/jscpd-sarif.json
          category: jscpd
```

### .github/workflows/dead-code-scan.yml

Report-only. knip has no base-branch diffing, so it cannot say what this PR orphaned.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. Report-only — knip lists the whole inventory and cannot say what
# THIS pull request orphaned. Every rule in knip.json is `warn`, so the exit code stays zero.
name: dead-code-scan

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "**/*.ts"
      - "**/*.tsx"
      - "**/*.js"
      - "knip.json"
      - "package.json"
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  dead-code-scan:
    name: Dead Code Scan (knip)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run knip
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          {
            echo '## knip'
            echo
            echo '```'
            yarn knip || true
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

### .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml

The one gate with no baseline. A committed key is already public, so there is nothing to grandfather and rotation is the only fix.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. A gate from the first run: unlike every other check this tool
# writes, there is no baseline and nothing is grandfathered. A key that has been committed is
# already public, and the fix is rotation rather than a commit.
name: secret-scan

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  # The scan only reads the checked-out repository.
  contents: read

jobs:
  secret-scan:
    name: Secret Scan (gitleaks)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The whole history is the point — a shallow clone misses the commit that leaked.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # The gitleaks CLI, not gitleaks-action: the action requires a licence key under a
      # GitHub Organization, while the CLI is MIT. The download is checksum-verified, because
      # fetching a scanner over the network unverified is its own supply-chain hole.
      - name: Install gitleaks
        env:
          GITLEAKS_VERSION: 8.30.1
          # Refresh alongside any GITLEAKS_VERSION bump, from the release page.
          GITLEAKS_SHA256: 551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ARCHIVE="gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
          curl -sSfL -o "$ARCHIVE" \
            "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/${ARCHIVE}"
          echo "${GITLEAKS_SHA256}  ${ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum -c -
          sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin -f "$ARCHIVE" gitleaks
          rm -f "$ARCHIVE"
          gitleaks version

      # `--redact` keeps the secret out of a log anyone can read. `.gitleaksignore` at the repo
      # root is honoured automatically. Exit 2 means findings; 1 also means gitleaks could not
      # run at all, and telling those apart is what stops a broken scan reading as a leak.
      - name: Run gitleaks over the full history
        run: gitleaks detect --source . --redact --verbose --exit-code 2
```

### .github/dependabot.yml

The lint stack is grouped: typescript-eslint's peer range pins which ESLint it accepts, so those bumps cannot merge separately.

```yaml
# Generated by ever-better. Keeps the pinned action versions and the lint stack current.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      eslint:
        patterns:
          - "eslint"
          - "eslint-*"
          - "@eslint/*"
          - "typescript-eslint"
          - "globals"

  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
```
